items.item_text: Education: High School graduate or the equivalent. Proof required. Supplemented by a minimum of 2 years college-level course work in social sciences or related field. Experience: Two years of responsible experience in the area of school social work, social advocacy or related fields. Computer literacy required. Must be proficient with Microsoft software, including but not limited to, Word, Excel, Access, Powerpoint, and other applications. LICENSES AND OTHER REQUIREMENTS: Valid California driver's license and a safe driving record.

Receive intra/inter-District transfer requests and assist in determining approval or denial. Assist parent/guardians in accurate completion of request forms. Contact schools for space available. Assist in maintaining and processing outgoing and incoming inter-district transfers and contracts with outside districts. Assist with Open Enrollment and related intra-district transfer processes. Prepare copies of requests and related information to schools and parent/guardians concering approval or denial as appropriate. Maintain accurate records related to transfers. Assist in redirect process. Contact schools for space available. Facilitate communication between district office, redirect school and home school. Maintain records of redirected students. Provide technical information to schools, programs, students, families and community on issues related to enrollment, attendance and truancy. Contact parent/guardians in person and on the telephone to obtain information regarding truant or absent students as assigned. Discuss issues related to irregular attendance and provide appropriate community resources to assist parent/guardian in resolving related issues. Prepare summary reports of contacts and notify appropriate school or district personnel of findings. Schedule and compile information for Student Attendance Review Board (SARB) hearings. Consult with schools regarding SARB process including required intervention and documentation. Notify parents, students and personnel of date and location of meetings. Compile student SARB cases for the hearings; attend meetings and hearings as requested and provide follow up support as needed. Issue appropriate forms to parents to verify residency and responsibility including declarations of parent and child residency, caregiver or guardianship, foster care placements, homelessness and related issues. Schedule and hold appointments for student enrollment and re-entry into the district. Assist parent/guardians with the completion of forms and input information into appropriate database. Inform parent/guardians and schools of policies and procedures related to enrollment and placement of students. Communicate with surrounding districts, schools, students, parents, and outside organizations including child protective services and law enforcement agencies to exchange information and resolve issues or concerns. Coordinate communications, resources and information to meet student needs and assure smooth and efficient program placement. Prepare and maintain accurate records and reports related to Child Welfare and Attendance activities including absence reports, SARB referrals and contracts, inter and intra-district transfers. affidavits to enroll students , records related to foster care and homeless students and other reports as assigned. Generate reports and distribute to appropriate school or district personnel; prepare and maintain student files and folders. Operate a variety of office equipment including a computer, telephone, copier, faxand other machines as assigned. Perform related duties as assigned. KNOWLEDGE AND ABILITIES: KNOWLEDGE OF: State and local laws, rules and regulations relating to student enrollment, attendance and transfers. District and school policies and procedures including objectives of assigned activities. Technical aspects of field of specialty. Effective community relations techniques and principles. Effective Oral and written communication skills. Interpersonal skills using tact, patience and courtesy. Record-keeping techniques. Operation of a computer terminal, data entry techniques and software related to responsibilities. Diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, and ethnic backgrounds of district students. ABILITY TO: Speak and write in Spanish (preferred). Perform technical duties relating to field. Establish and maintain cooperative and effective working relationships with others. Be flexible to perform work within changing priorities and possess sufficient interpersonal skill to work harmoniously with staff, students, administrators, parents and others. Plan and organize work. Meet schedules and timelines. Maintain records and prepare reports. Write clear and concise documents Operate a computer terminal to enter data, maintain records and generate reports. Determine appropriate action within clearly defined guidelines. Work independently with little direction.
